orchestrator_output.text_narration: The Cockroach Janta Party, or CJP, is a viral satirical youth movement in India that emerged in May 2026. It started as an online joke but quickly transformed into a massive social media phenomenon representing the frustrations of young, unemployed, and educated citizens. The movement was triggered on May 15, 2026, when the Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, made a remark comparing certain activists and unemployed youth with fake degrees to cockroaches and parasites. In response, a 30-year-old communications strategist named Abhijeet Dipke launched the Cockroach Janta Party on social media as a satirical protest. Within just 72 hours, the movement gained over two million followers, turning a moment of mockery into a powerful youth identity. While CJP uses humor and self-deprecation, calling itself the voice of the lazy and unemployed, it addresses serious systemic issues. Their five-point manifesto demands strict action against exam paper leaks like the NEET scandal, reforms in youth employment, 50 percent reservation for women in politics, freedom of the press, and a ban on post-retirement political rewards for judges. To support the movement and spread their message, CJP launched various products and merchandise. These include streetwear like oversized t-shirts and hoodies with slogans like 'Main Bhi Cockroach' and 'Unemployed but Immortal'. They also offer physical items like witty sticker packs, posters, and headbands, alongside digital products like personalized CJP member badges to fund their legal defense and campaign efforts.
